analysis: Reviewed scripts/test-provider-ci-workflow.py (head lines 1-785). The change is limited to an offline CI structure test: it adds PROVIDER_SHARDS=[1..5] (line 81) and updates test_lanes_are_independent_on_dedicated_supported_mac_runners (lines 195-225) and test_route_requests_exactly_one_lane_per_provider_shard (lines 227-233). These now assert that the provider job uses a matrix with fail-fast: false, per-shard route lanes (test-provider-N) and a runs-on lookup keyed by format('test-provider-{0}', matrix.shard), while SDK keeps a single lane and no strategy block. Nothing here touches provider runtime code, the coordinator WebSocket contract, key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization, prefix-cache storage or the add-on hold socket. No threat-model assets (A-001..A-019) or boundaries (TB-002..TB-013) are affected. The test only reads repository files and runs local stubbed subprocesses in temp dirs (no network, no secrets). It also asserts that the provider job has no secrets., coordinator or darkbloom-platform references, and no continue-on-error, which tightens CI integrity rather than weakening it. The assertions on the gate (needs [changes, test-provider, test-provider-summary], if always()) are retained and fail closed for non-success results. Remaining questions are outside the supplied evidence: the actual .github/workflows/ci.yml change and the route job were not supplied, so whether the workflow really matches these assertions (and whether per-shard routing changes runner trust or secret exposure) is unverified. This is a test-only change, not a security regression.
